title: Split-pane token blending and interactive control overrides for mixed-theme console
creator: Marina Cho
description:
Goal: define a repeatable token blending strategy and component override rules for 'split-pane' views where adjacent console panels may render different themes (e.g., left pane: light/brand; right pane: dark/compact). This ticket covers token interpolation at seams, focus/hover interactions for controls that cross the pane boundary, and a set of lightweight component overrides to avoid visual artifacts when two themes meet.

Scope: tokens (surface/ink/accent), interactive states for buttons/inputs/rows, table zebra inversion rules, and small component CSS overrides. Implementation guidance will be handed to engineering (ENG) with a small set of example tokens and a migration checklist for existing components.

Background: customers are building workflows that embed multiple console panels side-by-side (debugger/console, metrics/logs, playground). When teams configure different themes per-pane (brand vs neutral dark, or accessibility high-contrast vs default), seams currently show jarring borders, double shadows, or invalid focus rings. The goal is a predictable, low-cost approach that is easy to opt into from components and tokens, not requiring heavy per-component logic.
acceptance_criteria: A documented token blending algorithm (priority order + alpha mix rules) with examples for 3 common pairs: light+dark, brand-light+brand-dark, high-contrast+default
Buttons, inputs, and table rows that cross a pane seam render a single consistent hover and focus state without duplicated shadows
A dev-visible flag (data-split-seam) that components can read to apply the minimal override—no broader DOM surgery required
Table zebra inversion option implemented: when right-pane is dark, alternating row colors invert while preserving line contrast for focus/selection
Performance: no runtime layout thrash and no more than 2 additional CSS variables per component in the default build
Migration guide and 4 reference screenshots (left/right theme combos) uploaded to the design folder
design_notes: Use a deterministic blend: seamColor = mix(foregroundA, foregroundB, weight = seamWidth / (seamWidth + referenceDepth)). This keeps seam predictable when pane sizes change.
Prefer CSS variables for runtime overrides: --seam-surface, --seam-ink, --seam-accent. Components read these and fall back to local tokens if unset.
Interactive controls that overlap panes should prioritize the pane the pointer is over; if control anchoring is ambiguous, fall back to the focused pane's tokens.
Avoid elevation stacking at seams: replace drop-shadow with a thin divider token that adapts via seamSurface with low alpha instead of two shadows.
Table rows: implement 'zebra-invert' modifier that flips row surface deltas relative to pane base. Selection states use accent overlay with standardized 16% alpha to ensure legibility in both themes.
technical_dependencies: ENG-84555 (table rendering edge cases & accessibility testing)
discussion: 2026-02-19 - Marina: scoped initial research and prototypes. Built 3 visual examples in Figma: left-light/right-dark, left-brand/right-dark, left-highcontrast/right-default.
2026-02-22 - Liam: reviewed prototypes, requested clearer focus ring precedence when a focusable element straddles the seam. Suggested data attribute approach rather than DOM heuristics.

2026-02-25 - UX review: recommended removing heavy shadows at seams and adding a micro-divider token that adapts with seam alpha. Also asked for keyboard-only states to be validated (no pointer dependence).

2026-02-28 - Engineering sync (ENG-82410): agreed to expose three CSS vars from runtime and to land a tiny utility hook (useSeamTokens) in the component lib. Estimated implementation 3 engineers, 1 week.

2026-03-03 - Design update: finalized token names (--seam-surface, --seam-ink, --seam-accent) and published Figma components with tokens applied. Next: write migration guide and provide 4 annotated screenshots for QA.
